# Introduction

The **`alluvial`** analysis (Alluvial Diagrams) provides clinicopathological researchers and biostatisticians with intuitive, publication-ready tools in jamovi and R.

## Key Capabilities

- Draws an alluvial diagram: a flow picture of how cases move between the categories of several categorical variables. Ribbon width is the number of cases taking that path; with the GG Alluvial engine and a weight variable it is the total of that weight over those cases, while the Easy Alluvial engine always counts cases. Every axis variable is drawn with its own recorded values as the strata.
- Seamless integration between jamovi graphical interface and automated R syntax generation.
- Rigorous handling of missing data, small cohorts, and multi-variable stratification.

# Example Workflow in R

```r
library(ClinicoPath)

# Load package test dataset
data("alluvial_test", package = "ClinicoPath", envir = environment())

# Run analysis with default settings (add the required variable arguments
# for this analysis; see ?alluvial)
# ClinicoPath::alluvial(
#   data = alluvial_test
# )
```

# Clinical & Statistical Interpretation

Outputs generated by `alluvial` include summary tables, diagnostic indicators, and high-resolution plots tailored for oncology, pathology, and clinical trial reporting.
